samples.name: vantage-browser-153.5.0-1.src.tar.gz
samples.identification: AUR source build recipe for the Firefox/LibreWolf-derived Vantage browser
evidence: PKGBUILD fetches the upstream tag, prepares and patches Firefox sources with make dir, builds with a platform mozconfig, and packages browser binaries and a Desktop Entry. It explicitly uses make rather than invoking upstream build.sh.

Upstream build.sh registers an existing local build-monitor script every two minutes only when the script and crontab exist. It logs build output, records a PID, signs build products and checks their signatures. Its AppImage glob checks package signature sidecars; it does not chmod anything.

The updater PE contains an AutoHotkey script matching the shipped .ahk source after comments are removed. Its execution path retrieves vendor release metadata, chooses architecture-specific installer URLs and SHA256, verifies the installer hash, waits for the browser to close, and installs updates. Scheduling is exposed in the updater UI.

The standalone 7-Zip SFX is a stock extraction module without an appended archive. The MSIX remote helper uploads build artifacts to a configured authenticated packaging service and retrieves hash-checked MSIX output. Its counterpart invokes makeappx with fixed packaging arguments.
samples.correction: Fix the dependency traits directly, including the AppImage glob that falsely supplied executable-permission evidence. No package-specific exception was added.

samples.name: route-b-method.ps1
samples.decode: Add 704123 to each negative integer and cast to a character; execute the reconstructed source with ScriptBlock.Create(...).Invoke().
evidence: The decoded block compiles ConsoleApi P/Invoke declarations and calls ShowWindow(hwnd,0) and MoveWindow(hwnd,-10000,-10000,0,0,false) to hide the console.

It creates a GUID-named temporary directory and downloads an archive from orbitflownetwork.lol and 7zr.exe from the 7-Zip GitHub release. Archive magic and PE magic/length checks validate formats, not trust.

It runs 7zr hidden with a literal password, reads the inner password from an extracted text file, extracts a second archive hidden, then selects the first executable other than 7zr and launches it hidden.
The source attempts cleanup with Remove-Item on an environment-held script path. It also reassigns that path inside the dynamic block, so successful self-removal is not established.
samples.limits: The scanner does not recover this arithmetic layer automatically. Retain its two accurate suspicious concealment/evaluation traits; do not claim unsupported stealing or backdoor behavior of the unavailable next-stage executable.

samples.name: route-a-call.ps1
samples.decode: Add 704123 to each negative integer and cast to a character; invoke the reconstructed ScriptBlock using the call operator.
evidence: The decoded block configures WebClient with a browser-like User-Agent, downloads an MSI from an HTTP URL whose host is a decimal IPv4 address into a GUID-named temporary file, and retries download failures with randomized short delays.
It calls Unblock-File on the downloaded installer and invokes msiexec /i with /qn /norestart, concealing installer UI. The outer arithmetic encoding conceals this execution chain from inspection.
It attempts removal of the environment-held script path, with the same dynamic-invocation path-reassignment limitation as route B.
samples.limits: The MSI payload was not executed; no malware-family or downstream theft claim is made. The verdict rests on the concealed silent deployment and bypass behavior of the supplied script.
